First, numbers: a dye recipe is quoted in percent on weight of goods, so a chalked recipe board is the trade's own percent carrier and heritability, adolescent prevalence and recurrence can all be painted as recipe lines with their tag in the same hand, with no native unit competing (the quarry's depth plates could not do this — a plate reading 4 reads as metres). Second, hosting: the raphe weaving workshop is not imported into this venue, it is downstream of it — the yarn is dyed in these pits and carried straight through to the loom, which is exactly what the token means. Depression stays a literal hollow: the pits are holes in the floor, hanks go down into them and are lifted back out, and re-dipping a hank a second time to deepen the shade is the trade's own name for what recurrence is. venues.anchor_structure: The instrumented test run - the proof-load gantry with its load cell and figured dial carried on into the detector bench with its manifold and sounding alarms - crossing the frame from the lower left to the upper right and dividing the depot into the receiving bench, the test run, the tagging bench and the back wall of dated boxes.
venues.pun_explanation: GADD carries the acronym inside an ordinary family surname on an ordinary trade fascia, the Ben's Diner device, and nothing on the sign names the disorder. The premises are an inspection and issue depot rather than a kit shop: things arrive on their due date, go through a test and go back out with a dated tag on them, so the visual mass is instruments and paperwork, not racks of wearable stock. That trade is the chapter's core feature made literal. Worry spread across unrelated domains is one hazard to a line on the depot's own wall list - gas, height, fire, noise, eyes - so every domain hands over a separate prop with nothing invented. The paperwork is the numbers layer: the accident-free tally board is a chalked count of days and is the only carrier in the syllabus whose native unit is more days than not, every tag in the trade bears a due date and a six-month interval, and the inspection card is ruled into seven numbered check lines. The gantry and the detector bench give restlessness, muscle tension and startle as people literally under load and literally jumping when an alarm goes off. The almond-shaped personal panic alarms are ordinary stock in this trade, not a substitute for the token. And because the depot fronts onto a street, the bus stop stands where a bus stop stands, in view of the issue hatch.

venues.place: A radio repair shop on a quiet afternoon: a service counter with a docket spike at the front, a workbench under a swan-neck lamp with a chassis out of its cabinet, a shelf of sets awaiting collection with job tickets tied on, a valve index cabinet against the wall, and a public-address amplifier on soak test with a microphone on a stand.
venues.activity: Everyone is having a set looked at — carrying it in and setting it on the counter, saying out loud what it does wrong, standing back while it is switched on at the bench under the lamp, waiting for it to make a sound, collecting one off the shelf.
venues.anchor_structure: The long service bench with the shelf run above it — counter at one end, chassis and test gear along it, sets awaiting collection stacked overhead — cutting from the lower left of the frame to the upper right and splitting the shop into the public counter, the test bench, the parts wall and the soak-test corner.
venues.pun_explanation: The stock complaint of the repair trade is a set that plays perfectly at home and will not make a sound on the bench with the engineer watching, and that is selective mutism drawn as an ordinary Tuesday rather than as a symbol of one; the fascia takes one morpheme, SELECT, off the front of the diagnosis and lands it on selectivity, which is a real printed specification on radio sets, so the sign reads as a genuine shop name and never states the disorder. Social anxiety comes off the same bench as literal depiction: the whole business is being watched while your set is made to perform under a bright lamp, and a customer must state their name and their fault out loud to a stranger across a counter, which is the trigger the chapter is about. The public-address amplifier on soak test with its microphone carries the performance-only subtype in the manufacturer's own lettering, and a mute control on a faceplate is a redundant label on an object that already is that thing, which the corpus welcomes. The duration criteria have a native and non-competing carrier: repair dockets and guarantee slips are printed in months and spiked side by side, so the six-month and the one-month thresholds sit on two ordinary pieces of shop paper in the same hand. Deliberately not a studio and not a hi-fi showroom: this is a bench, a counter and a wall of dud valves.

The pun then pays out on every aspect without a single invented metaphor, because a welding shop already does, as routine work, everything this chapter teaches. A brief controlled current is passed through a workpiece that has been clamped so it cannot move: that is a tack weld and it is also the treatment. The choice the shop argues about all day is whether to run one side of the joint or both — single-sided against double-sided — which is unilateral against bilateral placement in the trade's own words. A course is a counted run of tacks chalked off on a tally board, not one long pass. The current dial and the ammeter are dose and threshold, and the strike current needed to establish the arc is the seizure threshold. The side effects are native too: the chalk setting-out marks burn clean off the steel either side of a seam and never come back, while fresh chalk will not take on hot metal at all — retrograde and anterograde amnesia rendered as one ordinary nuisance — and every welder in the frame is lifting a helmet and blinking at an after-image, which is post-ictal confusion by literal depiction. The comparators fit the same inventory: a magnetic drill working with no contact at all is induction, a regulated gas line is the anaesthetic, an earth cable clamped round the neck of a workpiece is a continuous stimulator, and an electrode driven deep into the middle of a thick block is the deep one. The apprentice permit board on the wall is the consent and minors question as posted shop regulation. The yard gate is declared adjacency: the rigid, red-hot piece that arrives from North Main Steel next door is the indication that walks in from the chapter next door.

venues.place: A canal lock on a working navigation, mid-morning: the stone chamber with its gates shut at the tail, balance beams swung out over the towpath, a queue of narrowboats waiting down on the low pound below with their propellers half out of the water, and the lock cottage with its porch bench and gauging tape at the top of the steps.
venues.activity: Everyone is working a boat through the lock: winding a paddle up one notch at a time on a windlass, leaning a balance beam round to swing a gate, holding a centre line while the chamber fills, watching the water climb the painted gauge board, and stepping off to set the next one.
venues.anchor_structure: The lock chamber wall itself — the long coursed stone face with its painted gauge board, ladder rungs, green water line and spalled mortar — running from the bottom-left of the frame to the top right, dividing the scene into the starved low pound with its waiting boats, the towpath and beams, the chamber, and the full pound above.
venues.pun_explanation: A lock exists to raise something starved of water back up to level, and the one absolute rule of working one is that you let the water in slowly, a notch at a time — draw all the paddles at once and the chamber boils in, the boat is thrown against the cill and holed. That is refeeding syndrome, drawn as the trade's own cardinal safety rule rather than as a metaphor, and it is the single hardest fact in the chapter to place anywhere else. The sign is the second half of the pun: on a canal a pound is the level stretch of water between two locks, and a pound short of water is the everyday phrase for a level that has run too low to float anything — while in trade a short pound is a pound that weighs less than a pound. One three-word place name that a canal would genuinely carry therefore says low weight twice, in two registers, and never says the diagnosis. The rest of the syllabus falls out of the stock: the subtypes are two boats, one that takes nothing on at all and one that fills its tank and then runs the bilge pump straight back over the side; the gauge board and the boat-gauging tape are the assessment instruments and also the disturbed reading of a hull that plainly fits and is recorded as too wide; bradycardia is the paddle wound at half speed, hypothermia the cold green water, the low electrolytes three low marks on the same board, and osteopenia the crumbling mortar of the chamber wall, which is the only structural thing in the frame and is losing it. Family-based treatment is the strongest image the venue supplies: a family works one boat through with the parents on the paddle gear controlling the rate of filling and the adolescent aboard, which is exactly the transfer of control FBT prescribes. Mortality is carried by the lifebelt, the rescue pole and the plate on the wall, and by the fact that this is the only venue in the batch where the ordinary hazard is drowning.

venues.place: A working cooperage on an ordinary morning: the test bay down the middle with a filling stand-pipe over a floor grating, casks standing on end along both walls with their gallonage stencilled on the head, and the raising fire and hoop-driving block at the far end. venues.pun_explanation: BULLIMORE is a real family name that carries B-U-L-I-M as an ordered subsequence in the expreSS tRIps manner and reads out loud as BULL-MORE, which is exactly what the word means — Greek bous limos, ox-hunger — so the fascia is the term's own etymology painted as a family firm and no clinical word appears on it. The trade is then the cycle itself: a cask is filled to the bung in one go and emptied down the grating in minutes, over and over, several times a week, and the register on the bench is ruled a line a week with the last twelve weeks ticked; and because a cask looks precisely the same full or empty from outside, this trade tests it by tapping it, which is why bulimia at an unremarkable weight is invisible unless you ask. The medical mimics are the cooperage's ordinary defects and are already chalked on the stock: staves eaten thin and pale on the inside where the liquid stood and the chime worn back (dental erosion), the pair of casks at the door swollen at the bilge with EASE HOOPS chalked on them (parotids), one split lengthwise at the head from being filled too hard (Mallory-Weiss), the potash drum run low (potassium), and every man's knuckles skinned by the hoop driver with the plaster tin left open beside it. Shape is what this trade judges everything by — the shape gauge is held to the bilge and a cask off shape is worth nothing however sound it is — and the one cask standing bunged and still full in the corner, chalked LEFT FULL, is the binge that is never got rid of.

venues.place: A small candle works with its dipping room open to the street on a seaside town's back parade, late afternoon: a row of heated wax vats down the middle, frames of wicks hanging over them from the overhead rail, the cooling rack along one wall, the burn-test bench beyond it and the packing counter at the sash window, with the deckchair lock-up at the end of the terrace and the five-storey hotel directly opposite.
venues.activity: Everyone is dipping tapers: lifting a frame of wicks off the rail, lowering it into a vat for a slow count, raising it and standing it on the cooling rack, then taking it round again — one thin layer at a time, over and over.
venues.anchor_structure: The long dipping bench — the run of heated wax vats with the overhead wick rail above it and the cooling rack alongside — crossing the room from the lower-left corner to the upper right, dividing it into the vats, the cooling rack, the burn-test bench and the packing counter at the street window.
venues.pun_explanation: A taper is a thin candle and a taper is the one instruction this chapter exists to give, and they are the same word, so a working candle shop puts the treatment rule on the fascia in the shop's own honest trade English. The device pays out because everything a taper does physically is what a dose schedule does: the burn-test bench carries a graded run of candles stepping down in height across the board, which is a written withdrawal schedule rendered as an object; and the one at the end that was snapped off and blown out instead of snuffed has flared, scorched the bench and put the fire bucket into the picture — an abrupt stop that turned dangerous, which is precisely why the chapter says withdrawal from this class can kill and alcohol-type withdrawal from any other cannot be assumed milder. The shop rules board carries the never-blow-one-out rule as posted regulation, which is the deontic half of the chapter. Cross-tolerance is a native fact of the trade rather than a metaphor: the same frames of wicks go into any vat on the bench, paraffin, stearin or beeswax, and the spirit bottle kept under the bench for thinning is the fourth thing that fits. The three drug families each get a prop family of their own — the graded tapers, three boxes stamped with Z's, and the barbed wire along the wall opposite — without any of them becoming the venue. The seafront back parade is a declared adjacency, not an accident: the deckchair hire at the end of the terrace is the prescribing chapter, and putting the use-disorder shop a few doors down the same parade is the corpus's barbershop-next-to-Cab-A move, where which building is next door is itself the teaching. It also puts the fixed five-storey hotel across the street as an ordinary seaside guest house rather than an imported structure.

venues.place: A high-street pawnbroker's on a Friday afternoon: a long counter with a brass grille, the redemption window at one end, a wall of racked guitars, watches and labelled unredeemed lots behind it, bicycles hung from the ceiling, and the shop door standing open onto the street with the amusement arcade opposite.
venues.activity: Everyone is pawning or redeeming something over the counter: unwrapping a watch out of a tea towel, watching it weighed and put under the loupe, taking a numbered ticket and counting the notes, or handing a ticket back through the grille and waiting while the lot is fetched.
venues.anchor_structure: The long mahogany pledge counter with its brass grille and the loaded ticket spike standing on it, running from the lower-left corner of the frame to the upper right, splitting the shop into the queue by the open door, the counter, the racked stock wall and the strong-room passage.
venues.pun_explanation: Both words on the fascia are ordinary pawnbroking and both are the chapter. Chase is a plain surname and chasing losses is the criterion that defines the disorder; a pledge is the object left over the counter and the pledge is what is taken at the Thursday meeting; and a pledge office is genuine trade English for the shop, so nothing on the sign is a joke a real high street would not carry. The venue was chosen over the obvious one because the casino is a fixed course-wide symbol and must stand inside the chapter's world, not replace it — so the world is the shop on the other side of the road, and the traffic between the two is the whole mechanism. Chasing is not asserted, it is drawn: the same watch redeemed and re-pawned, three stubs deep on the same spike, the customer going back out of the door and across. Tolerance is the escalating size of what comes in. The wedding ring in the tray is the relationship criterion and the parent at the counter paying off someone else's ticket is the bailout criterion, both of them literal depiction with no invented glyph. A pawnshop is also the only ordinary venue that keeps an explicit written list of what it will and will not take, which is where the DSM's decision lives: the dice are on the accepted list, and the games console sits in the locked cabinet with a not-yet label on it, because internet gaming is filed for further study rather than admitted. Treatment fits the same furniture — the small ad card in the window for the Thursday back-room meeting, the ledger where what was actually got back is written next to what was paid, and the bolt on the door. The stock inventory is enormous and every item on the shelf is a life someone has already handed over, which is a free fact-slot per object.

venues.place: A municipal model-yacht pond in a park on a Sunday morning: a paved perimeter walk right round the water, a small brick club hut with a glazed noticeboard beside its door, boat trestles set out along the path at wide intervals, and a low concrete island with a single tree standing in the middle of the pond.
venues.activity: Everyone is sailing a model yacht: standing at their own spot on the perimeter walk with a transmitter, trimming a sail, walking a few paces along the coping to follow the boat, lifting it out at the wall to shift the rig, and setting it back on the water.
venues.anchor_structure: The pond's long concrete rim and perimeter walk — the coping, the boat trestles ranged along it and the low island wall beyond — running from the bottom-left corner of the frame to the top right, splitting the scene into the club hut, the near walk, the open water with its island, and the far bank.
venues.pun_explanation: The pond's geometry is the disorder. Twenty people stand round one sheet of water doing exactly the same thing at exactly the same time, each rooted to his own arc of the coping, none of them closer than four paces to the next, and not one boat ever comes alongside another — present, parallel, permanently out of contact, and nobody in the frame is troubled by it. That is the distinction the chapter turns on, and the venue draws it rather than asserting it: the man on the far bank holding a boat he will not put on the water, watching a hut door he will not walk through, is Avoidant and he is plainly suffering; the men on the wall would not notice if the hut were open or shut, and that is Schizoid. The class name on the board does the retrieval work — Solo is a real single-handed class, so the fascia says solitary activities in the sport's own vocabulary without printing a diagnosis. The rest of the criteria are stock: one flask and one cup, a courting couple passing behind the trestles entirely unregistered, nobody smiling at a win, a member who reacts neither to the trophy shelf nor to the protest flag raised against him, and a flat face at a transmitter. The autism differential gets its own figure without a second venue — the member sailing the identical circuit over and over with his tools laid out in a rigid row is restricted and repetitive, which the others are not. Treatment is the coach who stands a deliberate two paces back and passes a spanner across without small talk. And the pond has, as an ordinary municipal feature, a small island with one tree on it, which is where the chapter's fixed glyph stands without being imported.

venues.place: A second-hand bric-a-brac shop on a small-town parade on Saturday, next door but one to the bowling alley: a long deal table of unsorted house-clearance boxes down the middle, rails of mismatched donated coats along one wall, and floor-to-ceiling shelves of crockery, lamps and paperbacks behind the counter. A child's play tipi is pitched in the toy corner at the back with a lamp burning inside it, and above the window display six old framed prints hang in a lettered row with a faceless dress form standing under them.
venues.activity: Everyone is rummaging — lifting things out of the boxes on the long table, turning them over for a price, trying the switch or winding the key to see whether it goes, and putting them back.
venues.anchor_structure: The long deal table of unsorted clearance boxes, running from the lower left of the frame to the upper right, dividing the shop into the window display and framed row, the rummaging aisle, the counter and shelves, and the toy corner with the tipi.
venues.pun_explanation: Typal to tipi is the course's own fixed derivation for this disorder and Tipi Top is the sort of cheery name a junk shop on a parade genuinely carries, so the fascia holds the phonetic hook while the actual tipi stands pitched at the back of the same room — the pun said twice, once in lettering and once in canvas. The shop was chosen because every object the fixed glyph needs is already its stock: the tarot deck under a rubber band, the crystal ball on a doily, the lava lamp, the dream catcher, the astrological chart and the four layers of donated clothing a rummage puts on a real customer's back, so odd appearance needs no inventing. The criteria hardest to draw are the ones the trade supplies best: the shoebox of second-hand greetings cards is a rack of messages addressed to a stranger in the second person — THIS IS YOUR DAY, SOMEONE IS THINKING OF YOU — and the customer standing with one of them open is idea of reference on pre-printed stock, doubled by the donated television plugged in to prove it works with its presenter apparently talking straight at her. The differential is native too: the foxed mirror and the crackling transistor are unusual perceptual experiences that anyone can check are simply a bad mirror and a bad radio, because nothing here is actually psychotic and everything works once you wind it. Treatment is on the tickets — the hand-written HOW IT WORKS card tied to the mangle, worked through step by step with a customer, is skills training done as shop routine, and the transistor left playing with its volume screwed right down under a ticket reading WORKS — TURN DOWN, NOT OFF, is the low-dose second line. The parade is a declared adjacency: the bowling alley two doors along is the schizophrenia chapter, several boxes on the table are lotted from the same house clearance as its raffle stock, and the spectrum relationship is drawn as which premises stand on the same street.

venues.place: A road-marking contractor's yard at half past seven on a working morning, the gates standing open onto the road. A towed thermoplastic boiler, a ride-on lining machine and a bead applicator are coupled nose to tail across the concrete; the drum store and stencil rack fill one side, and the mess hut with the job board stands by the gate. At the back a practice slab carries full-size sample lines laid in white, yellow and red.
venues.activity: Everyone is laying a line: stirring the boiler, snapping a chalk line and setting the road pins, walking the machine down the guide, dropping beads onto the wet material, kneeling to a stencil, then coning the work off until it sets.
venues.anchor_structure: The lining train — the towed thermoplastic boiler, the ride-on lining machine and the bead applicator coupled nose to tail — running from the lower left of the frame to the upper right and splitting the yard into the drum store, the machine run, the practice slab with its sample lines, and the mess hut and job board at the gate.
venues.pun_explanation: The fascia names the theorist exactly as an ordinary family contractor is named, in the corpus's own BOWLBY & SONS / MINUCHIN & SONS register with no clinical word painted anywhere, and the trade it names is the one trade on earth whose finished product is a border line laid down at full size — so the chapter's disorder is hosted rather than pointed at, while the yard pays the therapy out of its own statutory furniture: the printed order-of-markings chart that ranks stop line, then hazard line, then lane line is the target hierarchy already numbered on a real board, the day's lining sheet ruled into columns and filled in as they go is the diary card, the gang's briefing round the job board is the consultation team, the radio clipped in the lining cab is between-session coaching in a crisis, four stencil sets in numbered trays are the four skills modules, and the weather card that forbids laying below 5°C or on a wet surface is the acceptance half of the dialectic stated as a condition of work rather than as a slogan.

venues.pun_explanation: A can is a skull: rigid, sealed, opaque, and the only thing that shows from outside is the round stamped end, which loses its concentric rings and its sharp outer rim as the pressure inside rises — so the swollen disc is drawn on the venue's core prop and is felt by hand by every worker on the bench. venues.pun_explanation: Pawsey is a real surname over a real family yard and it says palsy; the initial in front of it is the one every such board carries, and the two together read without a clinical word being painted anywhere. The trade was chosen because its central operation is this chapter's whole management in one piece of everyday work: a plank is heated until it yields, bent round the frames, cramped home and left clamped until it cools, and it holds that shape for the life of the boat — while the one unclamped too early springs straight back. venues.pun_explanation: The chapter is practice questions and a weak-spot review, and a pub quiz is the one boring public place where strangers answer questions in rounds and then get their own marked sheet back. THE LAST ROUND is a completely plausible pub name and carries both meanings at once — the final round of questions and the last chapter of the course. The scoreboard column chalked 'MISSED' is the weak-spot review, the swapped-and-marked answer sheets are the retrieval drill, and the tie-breaker bell is the one question that decides it.
